study_identification_part.si4_title: Accommodating Site Variation In Neuroimaging Data Using Normative And Hierarchical Bayesian Models

cm1_clarity_of_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the goal to accommodate site effects in neuroimaging normative models by modeling site as random effects within hierarchical Bayesian models and comparing linear versus non-linear versions to improve performance.
cm1_clarity_of_research_objectives.supporting_text: "In this study, we suggest accommodating for these site effects by including them as random effects in a hierarchical Bayesian model. We compared the performance of a linear and a non-linear hierarchical Bayesian model in modeling the effect of age on cortical thickness."

nm1_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.reason: Healthy controls were drawn from the ABIDE dataset with counts provided (569 controls, 470 male) and basic quality control via outlier removal, but explicit inclusion/exclusion criteria for healthy status or detailed image quality rules beyond outlier screening are not described.
nm1_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.supporting_text: "The consortium provides a publicly available structural magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data set and corresponding phenotypic information of 539 individuals with autism spectrum disorder and 573 age-matched typical controls. For this study, we used 569 controls for development and performance testing of the models, out of which 470 were male."; "The measures were scanned for outliers. The criterion applied to mark a value as an outlier was if it was above or beyond 2 inter quartile ranges from the mean of all values for that region and hemisphere."
nm1_clarity_of_inclusion_and_exclusion_c.location: Bayer2022.pdf.md: 3.1.1 ABIDE data set; Bayer2022.pdf.md: 3.2 Pre-processing of the ABIDE data set
